messages:
maria.v: Heads up — nightly kernel-microbench flagged a regression+flake on candidate kernel 'k_alloc_v2' for H100 at seqlen=1024. p95 up ~+28% vs baseline, flakiness 3/10. Attaching perf-ci summary below.

perf-ci-bot: nightly-kernel-scan summary: job=kernel-microbench-archs, commit=abc123def, archs=[a100,h100], seqlens=[128,512,1024,2048], test=causal_attn_micro, result=regression on h100@1024, delta_p95=+28%, pval=0.02, failures=3/10, artifact=https://ci.redwood.internal/bench/abc123/report

chen.li: repro command (quick):
```
./bench/kernel_runner --model=gpt-neox-20b --arch=h100 --seqlen=1024 --batch=1 --kernel=k_alloc_v2 --iters=200 --profile=nvtx
```
ran this locally once and see the same ~25-30% p95 bump.

samir: triage notes: this only shows up on H100 runs at 1024+; A100 and CPU baselines look fine. Also saw occasional CUDA OOM warnings right before high-latency samples — could be transient allocator churn.

anya.p: saw this in traces too — the batching heuristic bumped to batch=4 for some runs because continuous-batcher grouped short bursts, which combined with seqlen=1024 pushes memory working set into fallback allocator path. Not surprising it's H100-specific (different memory paging behavior).

maria.v: perf snippet from failing run:
```
[bench] step 154: kernel=causal_attn_k_alloc_v2 launch_ms=11.9
[bench] step 155: kernel=kv_cache_read_ms=3.2 alloc_retry=true
[bench] step 156: kernel=causal_attn_k_alloc_v2 launch_ms=19.6  <-- p95 spike
[bench] step 157: kernel=kv_cache_write_ms=4.0
```
(Notice the alloc_retry flag and jump to ~19.6ms)

chen.li: hypothesis: autotuner selected k_alloc_v2 based on synthetic microbench at seqlen=512 and avg batch=1, but for seqlen=1024 with continuous batching it mispredicted. We should add seqlen-aware feature to kernel selector (prefer hybrid/fused kernels for >=1024).

samir: quick mitigation: pin fallback to k_classic_1024 for h100@1024 in rollout rules while we investigate. Also increase perf-ci sample size for h100@1024 to reduce flakiness noise.

anya.p: can confirm that switching to k_classic_1024 removes the p95 spike in my local runs. Suggest adding a small microbench that exercises KV cache eviction patterns (seqlen sweep + batch sweep + random prefix lengths).

maria.v: action items: 1) @chen.li run 8 seeds of the repro with nvprof + allocator traces and upload to the artifact. 2) @samir update rollout to pin k_classic_1024 for h100@1024 and disable k_alloc_v2 candidate for now. 3) Add a targeted microbench to nightly CI that sweeps seqlen=[512,1024,2048] x batch=[1,2,4] to catch this class. I'll open a PERF ticket.

perf-ci-bot: created PERF-2027: "h100@1024 p95 regression / k_alloc_v2 flakiness" linked: https://issues.redwood.internal/PERF-2027

chen.li: ack — starting repro runs now, will paste nvprof links in the ticket.

samir: I'll push the rollout pin and schedule the extra microbench sweep for the next nightly.

maria.v: thanks team. let's keep this thread for updates on the ticket and new CI runs. :slightly_smiling_face:
